title: Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba

paragraphs: In [Shabbat 126a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.126a.4) and [Moed Katan 5b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.5b.14), he speaks in Ulla’s name. In [Bava Batra 15a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.15a.6) and [Menachot 30a](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.30a.3-10), Rabbi Yehoshua bar Abba speaks in the name of Rav Gidel, who cites Rav. In [Yoma 42b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.42b.3-8) he raises an objection, which Abaye calls a refutation. Hyman infers that he preceded Abaye. From the consistent title Rabbi, Hyman infers that he was from the Land of Israel and studied there with Ulla and Rav Gidel, who later also lived there. Hyman cites [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1777&lang=en) for [Zevachim 32b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.32b.4), where his text reads Rav Hoshaya.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Moed Katan gives Rav Yehoshua bar Abba, while Shabbat, Bava Batra and Menachot give Rabbi. In Zevachim the consulted text names Rav Hoshaya; Heilprin suggests that an alternate “Rav Yehoshua” could be the sage in this entry.
